item.text:
Completed the review-round continuation for all eight chapter reviews (1B–8B), without scoring. The filesystem was read-only, so the supplied ledger and manifest paths could not be updated; append-ready material is below.

### New evidence items: R036–R052

- **R036 — 7B:** Tagesschau reported Scholz’s 19 August 2022 Cum-Ex testimony: he denied influencing Hamburg tax decisions, acknowledged three meetings with Warburg representatives, said he could not recall their contents, and faced criticism over “memory gaps.” [Tagesschau, lines 151–168](https://www.tagesschau.de/inland/scholz-cum-ex-105.html). Maps: `7B.1, 7B.2, 7B.6, 7B.7, 7B.10`. Direct statement and scrutiny; not proof of dishonesty.

- **R037 — 7B:** Tagesschau’s evidence review records unresolved diary allegations, the absence of an investigation against Scholz, disputed political influence, and reports of potentially deleted emails. [Tagesschau FAQ, lines 178–194](https://www.tagesschau.de/inland/innenpolitik/faq-cum-ex-warburg-100.html). Maps: `7B.3, 7B.4, 7B.6, 7B.7`. Adverse but unresolved; no finding of personal benefit or obstruction.

- **R038 — 7B:** Scholz stated in a September 2022 FAZ interview that investigations, witnesses, and documents had produced the same conclusion: no political influence. [SPD-hosted FAZ interview, lines 126–127](https://olaf-scholz.spd.de/aktuelles/detail/news/olaf-scholz-im-interview-mit-der-faz-1/06/09/2022). Maps: `7B.1, 7B.2, 7B.6, 7B.10`. Direct exculpatory statement; self-serving and requiring corroboration.

- **R039 — 7B:** NDR Panorama documented the Cum-Ex controversy, Scholz’s transparency commitment, meetings with Warburg officials, and diary-based questions. [NDR Panorama](https://www.ndr.de/fernsehen/sendungen/panorama/archiv/2022/Cum-Ex-Olaf-Scholz-und-die-Wahrheit%2Ccumex512.html). Maps: `7B.1, 7B.3, 7B.6, 7B.7`. Independent investigative reporting; allegations remain allegations.

- **R040 — 2B/8B:** Bundestag Scientific Services explains that German arms exports require Federal Government approval under Article 26 of the Basic Law; licenses are decided through the Economy Ministry using Foreign Office and Defence assessments, while contentious cases go to the secret Federal Security Council. [Bundestag Scientific Services PDF, pp. 1–3](https://www.bundestag.de/resource/blob/938170/12bc979cb7133464ad633f20565578ff/WD-2-016-23_EN-pdf-data.pdf). Maps: `2B.3, 2B.4, 2B.5, 2B.8, 2B.9, 8B.2, 8B.3`. Establishes formal authority and institutional constraints, not personal orders.

- **R041 — 2B/8B:** Foreign Minister Baerbock described allied coordination, support for Ukrainian self-defence, sanctions, humanitarian aid, weapons assistance, and secrecy intended to protect deliveries. [German Foreign Office, 27 April 2022](https://www.auswaertiges-amt.de/en/newsroom/news/2524258-2524258). Maps: `2B.1–2B.6, 2B.8, 2B.9, 8B.2–8B.6`. Official chronology and stated rationale; independent effects remain unresolved.

- **R042 — 2B/8B:** The Guardian reported contemporaneous criticism that the Chancellery reduced Ukraine’s requested heavy-weapons list and that Berlin delayed or ignored follow-up requests. [The Guardian, 21 April 2022](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2022/apr/21/german-report-casts-doubt-on-scale-of-its-weapons-support-for-ukraine). Maps: `2B.1, 2B.3, 2B.6, 2B.8, 2B.9, 8B.5, 8B.6, 8B.8`. Contrary evidence; reported claims require cautious attribution.

- **R043 — 2B:** Germany’s UN statement characterized Russian attacks on civilian infrastructure as deliberate violations of international humanitarian law. [German Mission to the UN, 6 December 2022](https://new-york-un.diplo.de/un-en/2567978-2567978). Maps: `2B.4, 2B.6, 2B.9`. Establishes government legal/diplomatic position, not independent adjudication.

- **R044 — 1B/8B:** The Federal Government’s cyber-security strategy specifies critical-infrastructure protection, state responsibilities, NATO/EU cooperation, monitoring, and adaptation mechanisms. [Federal Government cyber-security strategy](https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/service/archive/new-cyber-security-strategy-1958688). Maps: `1B.7, 1B.9, 8B.2–8B.6`. Pre-Scholz inherited-capacity context; not target-year ruler evidence.

- **R045 — 1B:** A search candidate for Baerbock’s August 2022 NPT statement indicated nuclear restraint and Germany’s TPNW observer decision, but the page could not be fetched with a precise locator. [Foreign Office search candidate](https://www.auswaertiges-amt.de/2545450). Maps provisionally: `1B.2, 1B.4, 1B.5, 1B.6, 1B.8`. `discovery_only`; not part of defensible evidence until retrieved.

- **R047 — 5B/6B:** The BMAS research report documents unusually high inflation from spring 2022 and explicitly examines household distributional effects. [BMAS research report](https://www.bmas.de/DE/Service/Publikationen/Forschungsberichte/fb-667-verteilungswirkungen-der-aktuellen-preisniveausteigerungen.html). Maps: `5B.8, 5B.9, 6B.1, 6B.3`. Context; does not establish Scholz attribution.

- **R048 — 5B/6B:** DIW estimated that energy prices caused a 3.4% average real-income loss, nearly 7% for the poorest decile, and found relief packages only partly offset the regressive burden. [DIW Berlin, 2022](https://www.diw.de/de/diw_01.c.840044.de/publikationen/wochenberichte/2022_17_1/hohe_energiepreise__aermere_haushalte_werden_trotz_entlastungspaketen_staerker_belastet_als_reichere_haushalte.html?pic=overview-figure1). Maps: `5B.1, 5B.3, 5B.8, 5B.9, 6B.1, 6B.3, 6B.6, 6B.8`. Independent contrary distributional evidence.

- **R049 — 6B/8B:** Eurofound records Germany’s €2bn federal support package for Ukrainian refugees, including housing, living expenses, childcare, schooling, health, and care, while noting Länder and municipal implementation responsibilities. [Eurofound PolicyWatch](https://static.eurofound.europa.eu/covid19db/cases/DE-2022-1_2232.html). Maps: `6B.2, 6B.3, 6B.4, 6B.6, 6B.8, 6B.9, 8B.2, 8B.3, 8B.6`. Formal implementation and distributed-authority evidence.

- **R050 — 6B/8B:** OECD documented refugee access to integration measures and work, while identifying housing constraints, dispersal rules, and social-assistance conditions. [OECD International Migration Outlook 2022](https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/international-migration-outlook-2022_30fe16d2-en/full-report/component-8.html). Maps: `6B.2, 6B.3, 6B.6, 6B.8, 8B.2, 8B.6`. Independent contextual and implementation evidence.

- **R051 — 6B/8B:** A joint BAMF/IAB/BiB/SOEP study based on approximately 11,200 interviews found that 17% of working-age Ukrainian refugees were employed, 92% of families with school-age children had at least one child in German school, and major needs remained language, employment, healthcare, and housing. [BAMF/IAB/BiB/SOEP, December 2022](https://www.bamf.de/SharedDocs/Anlagen/DE/Forschung/Kurzanalysen/kurzanalyse4-2022-ukr-gefluechtete.html?nn=282022). Maps: `6B.2, 6B.3, 6B.6, 6B.8, 6B.10, 8B.6`. Independent outcome evidence; attribution remains shared across federal, Länder, and municipal actors.

- **R052 — 3B/4B/6B:** Amnesty’s 2022 Germany report records inadequate investigations into racial profiling, lack of independent police complaint mechanisms, disproportionate protest restrictions, surveillance-law rulings, hate-crime increases, and refugee admissions. [Amnesty Germany 2022, lines 115–143](https://www.amnesty.de/informieren/amnesty-report/deutschland-2022). Maps: `3B.1, 3B.2, 3B.4, 3B.5, 3B.7, 3B.8, 3B.9, 4B.3, 4B.6, 4B.7, 4B.9, 6B.2, 6B.3, 6B.8`. Independent target-year evidence, but mostly institutional or subnational rather than Scholz-specific.

### Chapter disposition

- **1B:** Nuclear-specific evidence remains materially incomplete. The cyber strategy is inherited context; the NPT statement remains unverified. No usable evidence was found for command-and-control, nuclear safeguards, or catastrophic-risk governance.
- **2B:** Improved through independent legal-authority material, ministerial chronology, contrary reporting on heavy-weapons timing, and humanitarian-law framing. Arms end-use controls, civilian-impact assessment, energy dependence, and negotiation conduct remain open.
- **3B:** Amnesty adds target-year evidence on policing, protest restrictions, surveillance, hate crime, and complaint mechanisms. Federal/state responsibility and direct Scholz oversight remain unresolved.
- **4B:** Amnesty strengthens evidence on privacy, protest, and media/civic constraints, but no direct Scholz-specific opposition treatment, appointments, coalition self-binding, or digital-control decision was recovered. The EU Rule of Law page was discovery-only because retrieval returned HTTP 429.
- **5B:** Independent distributional evidence materially improves the inflation/relief record. Implementation audits, regional household outcomes, appointments, and responsibility for inherited energy dependence remain gaps.
- **6B:** Refugee-support implementation and service-user outcome evidence are substantially improved. Quality, affordability, regional variation, municipal capacity, and durability remain incomplete.
- **7B:** Direct statements and independent investigative reporting improve the personal-integrity record. The Cum-Ex controversy remains unresolved: no accepted source establishes personal benefit, concealment, obstruction, or a final judicial finding.
- **8B:** Refugee-support implementation and independent outcome data improve execution evidence. Coalition coordination, appointment/replacement decisions, adaptation after failures, and cross-portfolio outcomes remain weak.
